summary: Team Sky_captains has developed an advanced, landscape-optimized 3D/2D space mission simulator web application built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. The project features a dual Solo/Team command mode, 4 core NASA research categories (Earth Science, Heliophysics, Planetary Science, Astrophysics), 3 difficulty tiers (ISS, LEO/GEO, Deep Space), and a real-time 6-meter telemetry HUD (Mass, Power, Budget, Data, Comms, Time). It implements a rigorous 4-segment assembly trade-off engine (Space, Launch, Orbit, Ground) where players must balance scientific payload weight against rocket thrust and budget limits. Utilizing HTML5 Canvas animations and live space anomaly event handlers (such as Solar Storm mitigation), the application educates users on aerospace systems engineering through interactive gamification.
details: How it works: Players select an operational mode (Solo or 4-role Team), choose a NASA science category and difficulty tier, and enter a 4-segment assembly workbench. Here, they perform true aerospace trade-offs—balancing mass, power consumption, and financial budget across Space instruments (e.g., IM15 Camera, L3Harris Antenna), Launch vehicles, Orbits, and Ground stations. Features: Includes a Launch Verification check, live 2D Canvas flight simulation, and an interactive mid-flight Solar Storm Anomaly event where commanders must make critical emergency decisions. Tech Stack: Developed using HTML5, CSS3 (Neon-glow Cockpit Theme), JavaScript, and HTML5 Canvas API, hosted seamlessly on GitHub Pages for instant cross-platform mobile and desktop access. Intended Impact: To make complex aerospace engineering, resource trade-offs, and NASA open data accessible, engaging, and educational for students and space enthusiasts worldwide.
